body:
MAINLINE-037. QUESTIONABLE. 022d has not filed. The P2 lead is the full-named SR-200 scarf on CR-III 5056, least factor 1.006358. Faces work at 298.436 MPa, factor 1.156 on the 345 MPa tensile yield. At gamma 0.20 the same point is 0.33958 by global. In-band P3 is Mylar at 0.41179 by Perry and titanium with Kapton at 0.74170 by global. The 6.15 m and 5.5 m optima are outside the half-wave band.

The gradient is 1.7717 MPa per kelvin. A white coating, absorptance 0.20 and emittance 0.90, leaves 0.399 K and 0.707 MPa. Pattern bending is 0.818 MPa. The average rise is 3.48 K. Bare beryllium reaches 356.9 K and puts 621 kPa into the core, factor 0.388. Coated, that factor is 1.678 from the air temperature and 0.917 from the cold night. A complete sphere carries no membrane stress from the solar pattern.

The flight gust, 35 ft/s at 35 knots, leaves the lead at 1.003303. Table 4's 70-knot wind, mapped as a uniform excess, leaves 0.998442. The 016 mooring load is 48.259 kN. The bare patch is factor 0.354. One pad, 0.200 m2 and 8.65 kg, restores crush to 1. The 70-knot pad is 33.1 kg.

Sun and wind leave the in-band P3 factors at 0.41051 and 0.74123. Wall area to reach 1 is 5863 kg and 1634 kg, more than the lift can take. The open choices are the coating, the bond temperature, and the mooring wind. No next job.
